To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the disaster-to-sustainability framework is an important tool for identifying and analyzing the factors that influence sustainability transitions following a disaster.

(i) the analytical framework developed in this study is an important tool for understanding the opportunities for sustainability transitions that arise in the aftermath of disasters; (ii) the framework is useful in documenting, analysing, and comparing disaster-to-sustainability transition cases; (iii) the framework can serve as a tool for guiding the design of interventions to support sustainability transitions in post-disaster settings; and (iv) the framework can help to develop theory on disaster-to-sustainability transformations.
disasters are catalysts for sustainability transitions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make disasters work towards sustainability, and how to make sustainability work following disasters.
the following questions: How can we better understand the potential of disasters to facilitate sustainability transitions?
the following: 1) How do disasters trigger change towards sustainability objectives?

the study has developed a unified framework to facilitate the understanding of disaster-to-sustainability transition processes, and that the framework is applicable to different disaster contexts.
disasters provide opportunities to achieve sustainable development goals, and that this can be done through a combination of disaster management and sustainability science approaches.
the framework can be used to identify and understand the conditions, resources and social relations that affect disaster-to-transition opportunities, and to identify constraints to their realization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
disasters can be a catalyst for change towards sustainability.
